reason: The goal calls for folding a corner, and the paper is the piece with marked corners.

reaction: The description makes the physical change clear.
reason: The new goal calls for another fold, so I will use the paper at Fold again.

effect: The second fold leaves two flat corners, and the next goal calls for folding the third.
reaction: The description clearly shows the build progressing.
reason: The same paper and Fold action have worked for both previous corners.
expectation: A third corner will curl inward toward the centre.

effect: Three corners are folded, leaving one flat corner to finish.
reaction: The remaining corner is clearly identified, though the repeated folds are predictable.
reason: The last corner needs the same fold as the previous three.
expectation: The last corner will curl inward toward the centre.

effect: The final fold made the paper into four blades, and the next goal is to fit the hub.
reaction: It is satisfying to see the repeated folds become a recognizable blade assembly.
reason: The goal explicitly calls for fitting the hub to the blades.
expectation: The green hub will attach at the centre of the blades.

effect: The hub is now fitted over the centre, and the next goal is to turn the blades over.
reaction: The green cap makes the assembly visibly closer to the reference.
reason: The goal explicitly calls for flipping the blades, and Flip is an available hotspot.
expectation: The blade assembly will turn over to expose its back.

effect: Flipping exposed the back of the blades and the hub tip for the axle.
reaction: The change of side and the next attachment point are clear.
reason: The goal calls for fitting the axle into the hub on the back of the blades.
expectation: The axle will attach to the back of the hub.

effect: The axle is fitted to the back of the blades, leaving its stem available for the handle.
reaction: The projecting stem makes the next connection clear.
reason: The goal explicitly calls for clipping the handle onto the axle.
expectation: The handle will clip onto the axle behind the blades.

effect: The handle is attached, forming the pinwheel; it now needs to be turned to the front.
reaction: The assembled handle brings the construction close to the reference.
reason: The new goal explicitly calls for flipping the pinwheel.
expectation: The pinwheel will turn to show its front.

effect: The final flip revealed the completed pinwheel and showed that its blades turn while the handle stays still; all goals are complete.
reaction: The moving blades are a satisfying payoff to the assembly, although text alone cannot establish how the artwork looks or the toy feels.

mostWorthwhile.text: Fitting the handle brought the separate parts together into a recognizable pinwheel, setting up the final motion reveal.

leastWorthwhile.text: The repeated corner folds were clear and showed incremental changes, but became predictable.

surprise.text: The final presentation showed the blades turning around a stationary handle, making the axle's purpose clearer.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary: each goal named the next operation, and the described changes supported it.

continue.text: I would be mildly interested in another chapter to see a different construction, though the very guided, repetitive folds offered few meaningful choices.
